summary: A short note from the UCSB Computer Research Lab saying its 360-75 got a new production network interface, replacing the older one, which began operation on May 1, 1972. It resembles the units used at NASA Ames and USC. Users are asked to report any trouble that might relate to it.

plainLanguage.summary: UCSB replaced the network interface for its 360-75 with a production unit like those at NASA-Ames and USC. The lab asked users to report any related problems.

questions: what changed in the ucsb 360-75 network interface
subtitle: A replacement network interface for the UCSB 360-75

tldr.problem: UCSB replaced the network interface previously used by its 360-75.
tldr.mechanism: A production unit similar to the interfaces at NASA-Ames and USC went into operation on May 1, 1972.
tldr.outcome: UCSB asked network users to report problems that might be related to the new unit.

today: RFC 335 is a brief notice about a replacement network interface at UCSB. Its text records when the unit entered operation and asks users to report possible problems.

sections.title: The New IMP Interface
sections.content: The UCSB 360-75's former interface to the network was replaced by a production unit similar to the units at NASA-Ames and USC. The replacement controller went into operation on May 1, 1972.
sections.plainLanguage: UCSB installed a production replacement for the unit connecting its 360-75 to the network. It began operating on May 1.

sections.title: Reporting Problems
sections.content:
Roland Bryan and the UCSB Computer Research Lab asked network users to report difficulties they encountered while communicating with UCSB if those problems might be related to the replacement interface.

The notice does not describe a specific fault or claim a measured improvement.
sections.plainLanguage: Users were asked to tell UCSB about connection problems that might involve the new interface. The notice does not say that a particular problem had occurred.

sections.title: A Brief Change Notice
sections.content: This RFC is a short operational announcement. It identifies the replacement equipment as a production unit and gives the date it began operating, without describing its detailed design.
sections.plainLanguage: The note records a hardware change and invites reports from users. It does not provide technical details about how the interface works.
